messages:
Maya R.: Heads-up: product is aiming for a BF-ish promotion window 72h after next deploy. Traffic sim shows a ~5.8x peak vs baseline for inference requests. Need a quick ops/infra triage: GPU hours, regional buffer, fallback plan, and cost delta. Who can run a runbook sim and surface the cheapest safe config by EOD?
Jon H.: I can run a capacity sim. Asking: do we keep dedicated reserved for NA and EU only, or include APAC (limited region) for spillover?
Vikas P.: Recommend reserve NA primary, EU secondary. APAC should be cold-fallback only — networking egress and PCIe topology there adds latency.
Sasha K.: Agree on NA/EU primary. Also we should prewarm KV cache and prefix cache for frequent prompts. Prewarm reduces tail latency a lot with <12hr warm window.
Rachel L.: Running a quick back-of-envelope: baseline monthly GPU hours = 45,200. If peak is 5.8x over a 6h hot window, additional GPU-hours ~ (5.8-1)*baseline*(6/24) roughly 45.2k * 4.8 * 0.25 = ~54k extra for that day. For multi-day promo multiply accordingly.
Lee M.: Cost delta: with spot-heavy mix we'd save ~30% on GPU compute but risk preemptions during sustained hot path. If SLA requires <200ms p95, avoid spot for the hot pool.
ops-bot: perf-alert: last 24h p95 gen latency NA = 142ms, EU = 160ms, baseline util NA = 36%.
Jon H.: I ran the sim (quick script): throughput target 12k tok/s sustained. Options I modeled: reserved-only, reserved+spot-burst, reserved+cross-region-fallover. Results: reserved-only needs +28% cores (GPUs) -> +63k GPU-hours for promo; reserved+spot-burst saves ~22k GPU-hours but adds 12-18% request failures in worst-case preemptions; reserved+cross-region-fallback uses cold APAC and saves ~10k hours but increases median latency by ~30ms for fallback routed requests.
Sasha K.: Important: fallback routing will hit inter-region egress; estimate 25GB/s cross-region at peak which could trigger cloud egress caps and cost. Need to add bandwidth headroom.
Rachel L.: Putting numbers: extra GPU-hours for single-day promo (reserved-only) = 63,000; estimated incremental compute cost = $195k (on committed reserved pricing), spot-burst variant incremental compute cost = $137k plus retry handling dev cost. Cross-region fallback incremental = $160k + ~$12k egress.
Vikas P.: Ops trade: if we commit to reserved for NA/EU now, we can lock in price and remove spot risk. Can also set autoscale conservative min/max to reduce cold starts. Propose: min pool = 20 GPUs, hot pool target = baseline *1.4, burst pool = reserved spare capacity.
Jon H.: Pushing a small config snippet for the autoscaler that I tested locally:
```
autoscaler:
  minReplicas: 20
  maxReplicas: 140
  targetUtilization: 0.7
  prewarmSeconds: 1200
  overflowPolicy: "fallback-to-eu"
```
Sasha K.: PrewarmSeconds = 1200 (20m) helps per-request tail when scaling quickly, but real benefit at 10-15m. For BF we should run 4-6h prewarm sweep across hot model variants and largest sequence lengths.
prometheus-bot: sim-metrics: sim_id=bf-sim-2026-04; peak_inference_rps=12.1k; peak_gpu_util=92%; cross_region_egress=24.6GB/s; estimated_failure_rate_spot=13%.
Lee M.: Ops checklist proposal: 1) Approve reserved commit for NA/EU to cover +30% hot capacity. 2) Configure autoscaler as Jon suggested with conservative ramp. 3) Run 8h prewarm job 6h before window across hot-models. 4) Enable cross-region fallback but throttle to 10% of traffic and alert for egress > 20GB/s. 5) Pair with runbook for graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model family).
Maya R.: +1 Lee's checklist. Action items: Jon run final sim with 1-day and 3-day promo shapes and attach cost delta. Vikas coordinate reserved commit terms with finance. Sasha schedule prewarm jobs and KV cache warms. Rachel prepare a short note for PMs on latency tradeoffs. We'll reconvene in this thread at 18:00 PST. :thumbsup:
Jon H.: On it. ETA 16:30 PST for sims.
Vikas P.: I'll ping finance and legal.
Sasha K.: KVs scheduled, I'll post run IDs.
Maya R.: Thanks all — keep replies short in thread. If latency spikes during promo, follow the degradation play (shrink model family -> enable cached responses -> rate-limit non-critical routes).
